claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few questions.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is in full-time education - he's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college would generally count as non-advanced education.

To confirm his eligibility, I need to know: when did Alex turn 18, and is he still enrolled in his A-level course? (Child Benefit can continue until the 31st August after a young person turns 18 if they remain in approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 earlier this year, and yes, he's still enrolled in his A-levels. He's got another year to go before he finishes them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and are responsible for his upbringing and care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me, and I'm responsible for his care and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

Do you normally live in the UK? (This is important for determining eligibility for Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

Is there anyone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 18, he's still in full-time non-advanced education (his A-levels at sixth form college), which means you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him until the 31st August following his 18th birthday, or until he finishes his course - whichever comes first.

✓ **You meet the requirements** - You live with Alex in the UK, you're responsible for his care, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

Since Alex turned 18 earlier this year and is continuing his A-levels with another year to go, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for him through to 31st August next year (or until he completes or leaves his course if that's sooner).

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, it should continue as long as Alex remains in approved education and the conditions above continue to be met.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
